rules.description: There shall be no occurrence of undefined or critical unspecified behavior.
rules.rationale: Safety, Security, Refer to Ref. [2] Rule 1.3,
rules.notes: According to used C11 Standard version (Ref. [3], [4]) there are some defined undefined behaviors. This rule prevents any of those undefined behaviors that occur in the code.

rules.description: A project shall not contain unreachable code.
rules.rationale: Safety, Refer to Ref. [2] Rule 2.1, Refer to Ref.[1] 6.4.4.3.c
rules.notes:
Each code piece is to perform an intended behavior. Any unreachable i.e. extraneous code shall be removed from executable object file.
As an example, cases like default: clause in switch case shall be caused by a requirement otherwise it is considered extraneous.

rules.description: A project shall not contain dead code.
rules.rationale: Safety, Refer to Ref. [2] Rule 2.2, Refer to Ref.[1] 6.4.4.3.c
rules.notes: Each code piece is to perform an intended behavior. Any unreachable i.e. extraneous code shall be removed from executable object file.

rules.description: A project shall not contain unused type declarations.
rules.notes: If a type is declared but not used, then it is unclear to a reviewer if the type is redundant or it has been left unused by mistake.

rules.description: A project shall not contain unused tag declarations.
rules.notes: If a tag is declared but not used, it is unclear whether the declaration is redundant or was left unused by mistake. This may reduce readability and complicate review.

rules.description: A project shall not contain unused macro definitions.
rules.notes: If a macro is defined but not used, then it is unclear to a reviewer if the macro is redundant or it has been left unused by mistake.

rules.description: A function shall not contain unused label declarations.
rules.notes: If a label is declared but not used, then it is unclear to a reviewer if the label is redundant or it has been left unused by mistake

rules.description: A function shall not contain unused parameters.
rules.notes: Most functions will be specified as using each of their parameters. If a function parameter is unused, it is possible that the implementation of the function does not match its specification. This rule highlights such potential mismatches.

rules.description: A project shall not contain unused object definitions.
rules.notes: If an object is defined but unused, then it is unclear to a reviewer if the object is redundant or it has been left unused by mistake.

rules.description: The character sequences /* and // shall not be used within a comment.
rules.notes: If a comment starting sequence, /* or //, occurs within a /* comment, is it quite likely to be caused by a missing */ comment ending sequence. If a comment starting sequence occurs within a // comment, it is probably because a region of code has been commented-out using //.

rules.description: Line-splicing shall not be used in // comments.
rules.notes:
The source line containing a // comment ends with a \ character in the source character set, the
next line becomes part of the comment. This may result in unintentional removal of code.

rules.description: Octal and hexadecimal escape sequences shall be terminated.
rules.notes: If the source line containing a // comment ends with a \ character in the source character set, the next line becomes part of the comment. This may result in unintentional removal of code.

rules.description: Trigraphs shall not be used.
rules.notes: Trigraphs are sequences of three characters that start with two question marks (??) and represent a single character. They were introduced in early C standards to allow programmers to type certain characters on keyboards that didn’t have them (e.g., {, }, #).

rules.description: External identifiers shall be distinct.
rules.notes:
In C99 and later the minimum requirement is that the first 31 characters of external identifiers are significant, with each universal character or corresponding extended source character
occupying between 6 and 10 characters.

rules.description: Identifiers declared in the same scope and name space shall be distinct.
rules.notes: In C99 and later the minimum requirement is that the first 63 characters are significant, with each universal character or extended source character counting as a single character.

rules.description: An identifier declared in an inner scope shall not hide an identifier declared in an outer scope.
rules.notes: In C99 and later the minimum requirement is that the first 63 characters are significant, with each universal character or extended source character counting as a single character.

rules.description: Macro identifiers shall be distinct.
rules.notes: If macro identifiers are not distinct, preprocessing results may become ambiguous and difficult to review.

rules.description: Identifiers shall be distinct from macro names.
rules.notes: Reusing the same name for both a macro and an identifier may cause confusion and unexpected preprocessing behavior.

rules.description: A typedef name shall be a unique identifier.
rules.notes: Unique typedef names improve clarity and prevent confusion in declarations and interfaces.

rules.description: A tag name shall be a unique identifier.
rules.notes: Unique tag names prevent ambiguity in structure and enumeration declarations.

rules.description: Identifiers that define objects or functions with external linkage shall be unique.
rules.notes: External linkage identifiers are visible across translation units; therefore, uniqueness shall be preserved project-wide.

rules.description: Identifiers that define objects or functions with internal linkage shall be unique.
rules.notes: Although internal linkage limits visibility to one translation unit, unique naming is still recommended for maintainability and reviewability.

rules.description: A reserved identifier or reserved macro name shall not be declared.
rules.notes: Reserved identifiers and macro names may conflict with compiler, standard library, or toolchain internals and shall therefore be avoided.

rules.description: A “u” or “U” suffix shall be applied to all integer constants that are represented in an unsigned type.
rules.notes: Applying the correct unsigned suffix makes the intended type explicit and helps prevent implicit signed/unsigned conversion issues.

rules.description: The lowercase character “l” shall not be used in a literal suffix.
rules.notes: The lowercase letter “l” can easily be confused with the digit “1”, reducing readability

rules.description: A string literal shall not be assigned to an object unless the object’s type is “pointer to const-qualified char”.
rules.notes: String literals are not modifiable; assigning them to a non-const-qualified pointer may lead to undefined behavior.

rules.description: The argument of an integer constant macro shall have an appropriate form.
rules.notes: Integer constant macros shall be written in a form that clearly preserves the intended width and signedness.

rules.description: The small integer variants of the minimum-width integer constant macros shall not be used.
rules.notes: Use of small integer constant macro variants may reduce portability and increase the likelihood of unintended type-related behavior.

rules.description: Types shall be explicitly specified.
rules.notes: Explicit type specification improves readability and avoids ambiguity in declarations and interfaces.

rules.description: Function types shall be in prototype form with named parameters.
rules.notes: Prototype form with named parameters improves interface clarity, enables stronger type checking, and supports safer function usage.

rules.description: All declarations of an object or function shall use the same names and type qualifiers.
rules.notes:
Using types and qualifiers consistently across declarations of the same object or function encourages stronger typing.
Specifying parameter names in function prototypes allows the function definition to be checked for interface consistency with its declarations.

rules.description: A compatible declaration shall be visible when an object or function with external linkage is defined.
rules.notes: A prior compatible declaration makes the interface explicit and enables consistent type checking across translation units.

rules.description: An external object or function shall be declared once in one and only one file.
rules.notes: Declaring each external object or function in one and only one file improves interface control and avoids inconsistent declarations.

rules.description: An identifier with external linkage shall have exactly one external definition.
rules.notes: Multiple external definitions may cause linkage conflicts and unpredictable behavior at build or run time.

rules.description: The static storage class specifier shall be used in all declarations of objects and functions that have internal linkage.
rules.notes: Consistent use of static makes internal linkage explicit and prevents unintended external visibility.

rules.description: An object shall be declared at block scope if its identifier only appears in a single function.
rules.notes: Block-scope declarations reduce visibility, improve readability, and limit unintended use outside the relevant function.

rules.description: An inline function shall be declared with the static storage class.
rules.notes: Declaring inline functions as static avoids multiple-definition issues and improves portability across translation units.

rules.description: All declarations of an object with an explicit alignment specification shall specify the same alignment.
rules.notes: Inconsistent alignment specifications for the same object may cause incorrect assumptions about storage layout and access.

rules.description: There shall be no tentative definitions in a header file.
rules.notes: Tentative definitions in header files may lead to multiple definitions when the header is included in more than one translation unit.

rules.description: The value of an object with automatic storage duration shall not be read before it has been set.
rules.notes: Reading an automatic object before initialization may result in indeterminate values and unsafe behavior.

rules.description: The initializer for an aggregate shall be enclosed in braces.
rules.notes: Braced initializers make aggregate initialization explicit and easier to review.

rules.description: Arrays shall not be partially initialized.
rules.notes: Partial initialization may hide unintended default values and shall be avoided in safety-critical code.

rules.description: Operands shall not be of an inappropriate essential type.
rules.notes: Inappropriate essential types may cause unintended conversions, loss of meaning, or incorrect runtime behavior.

rules.description: Expressions of essentially character type shall not be used inappropriately in addition and subtraction operations.
rules.notes: Character types shall not be used as small integers unless this usage is explicit and well justified.

rules.description: The value of an expression shall not be assigned to an object with a narrower essential type or of a different essential type category.
rules.notes: Assignment to a narrower or different essential type category may lose information or change the intended interpretation of the value.

rules.description: Both operands of an operator in which the usual arithmetic conversions are performed shall have the same essential type category.
rules.notes: Mixing different essential type categories in arithmetic expressions may produce unexpected conversion results.

rules.description: The value of a composite expression shall not be assigned to an object with wider essential type.
rules.notes: Assigning a composite expression to a wider essential type may conceal earlier type-related issues in the expression.

rules.description: If a composite expression is used as one operand of an operator in which the usual arithmetic conversions are performed then the other operand shall not have wider essential type.
rules.notes: Using a wider operand together with a composite expression may introduce unexpected implicit conversions.

rules.description: The value of a composite expression shall not be cast to a different essential type category or a wider essential type.
rules.notes: Casting a composite expression to a different essential type category or a wider essential type may hide loss of precision or type interpretation issues.

rules.description: Conversions shall not be performed between a pointer to a function and any other type.
rules.notes: Conversions between function pointers and other types are non-portable and may result in undefined or unsafe behavior.

rules.description: Conversions shall not be performed between a pointer to an incomplete type and any other type.
rules.notes: Such conversions are non-transparent and may lead to unsafe or non-portable behavior.

rules.description: A conversion shall not be performed between a pointer to object type and a pointer to a different object type.
rules.notes: Converting between unrelated object pointer types may violate type assumptions and cause undefined behavior.

rules.description: A conversion shall not be performed between a pointer to object and an arithmetic type.
rules.notes: Pointer–integer conversions are implementation-dependent and shall be avoided except where explicitly justified by the target environment.

rules.description: A cast shall not be performed between pointer to void and an arithmetic type.
rules.notes: Such casts reduce portability and may break assumptions about address representation.

rules.description: A conversion shall not remove any const, volatile or _Atomic qualification from the type pointed to by a pointer.
rules.notes: Removing qualifiers may bypass intended access restrictions and invalidate design assumptions.

rules.description: The macro NULL shall be the only permitted form of integer null pointer constant.
rules.notes: A single null-pointer representation improves consistency and readability.

rules.description: Pointers shall not be implicitly compared to NULL.
rules.notes: Explicit comparison improves readability and makes pointer intent clear during review.

rules.description: The precedence of operators within expressions shall be made explicit.
rules.notes: Explicit grouping with parentheses reduces ambiguity and review errors.

rules.description: The right hand operand of a shift operator shall lie in the range zero to one less than the width in bits of the essential type of the left hand operand.
rules.notes: Out-of-range shift counts may cause undefined or implementation-dependent behavior.

rules.description: The comma operator shall not be used.
rules.notes: The comma operator obscures intent and reduces readability.

rules.description: The sizeof operator shall not have an operand which is a function parameter declared as “array of type”.
rules.notes: Such parameters are adjusted to pointers, which may mislead the developer about the actual size being evaluated.

rules.description: The value of an expression and its persistent side effects shall be the same under all permitted evaluation orders and shall be independent from thread interleaving.
rules.notes: Expressions shall not rely on unspecified evaluation order or concurrent side-effect interactions.

rules.description: A full expression containing an increment (++) or decrement (--) operator shall have no other potential side effects other than that caused by the increment or decrement operator.
rules.notes: Restricting side effects in such expressions improves clarity and prevents subtle evaluation-order issues.

rules.description: The result of an assignment operator shall not be used.
rules.notes: Using assignment results inside larger expressions reduces readability and may hide defects.

rules.description: The right hand operand of a logical && or || operator shall not contain persistent side effects.
rules.notes: Short-circuit evaluation may suppress side effects and create control-flow-dependent behavior.

rules.description: The operand of the sizeof operator shall not contain any expression which has potential side effects.
rules.notes: Side effects inside sizeof operands are misleading because the operand is not normally evaluated.

rules.description: The software shall not use floating-point data types or constants and operations.
rules.notes: The project shall target a CPU that does not provide an FPU. Therefore, the additional math library is prevented from being used.

rules.description: A for loop shall be well-formed.
rules.notes: A well-formed for loop improves analyzability, readability, and predictability of iteration behavior.

rules.description: Controlling expressions shall not be invariant.
rules.notes: Invariant controlling expressions may create unintended infinite loops or unreachable branches.

rules.description: The controlling expression of an if statement and the controlling expression of an iteration-statement shall have essentially Boolean type.
rules.notes: Boolean controlling expressions make decisions explicit and reduce implicit-conversion issues.

rules.description: The goto statement shall not be used.
rules.notes: goto complicates control flow and makes code more difficult to analyze and maintain.

rules.description: A function shall have a single point of exit at the end.
rules.notes: A single exit point simplifies review, tracing, and control-flow analysis.

rules.description: The body of an iteration-statement or a selection-statement shall be a compound-statement.
rules.notes: Mandatory braces prevent accidental misbinding and improve readability during maintenance.

rules.description: All switch statements shall be well-formed.
rules.notes: Well-formed switch constructs improve analyzability and reduce fall-through-related defects.

rules.description: A switch label shall only be used when the most closely-enclosing compound statement is the body of a switch statement.
rules.notes: This restriction preserves proper control-flow structure and prevents misleading label placement.

rules.description: Every switch-clause shall be appropriately terminated.
rules.notes: Proper termination prevents unintended fall-through and clarifies control flow.

rules.description: Every switch statement shall have a default label.
rules.notes: A default label ensures that unexpected values are handled explicitly.

rules.description: Every switch statement shall have at least two switch-clauses.
rules.notes: Very small switch statements are often clearer when expressed using simpler control constructs.

rules.description: A switch-expression shall not have essentially Boolean type.
rules.notes: Boolean decisions are generally clearer and safer when expressed using if statements.

rules.description: Functions shall not call themselves, either directly or indirectly.
rules.notes: Recursion complicates stack usage analysis and may be unsuitable for constrained embedded systems.

rules.description: A function shall not be declared implicitly.
rules.notes: A function shall be declared before it is used so that the compiler can perform proper type checking and interface validation.

rules.description: All exit paths from a function with non-void return type shall have an explicit return statement with an expression.
rules.notes: Every return path shall make the returned value explicit and reviewable.

rules.description: The function argument corresponding to a parameter declared to have an array type shall have an appropriate number of elements.
rules.notes: Insufficient array size may cause out-of-bounds access or interface misuse.

rules.description: The value returned by a function having non-void return type shall be used.
rules.notes: Ignoring a return value may discard status, diagnostic, or computed information required by the design.

rules.description: A function parameter shall not be modified.
rules.notes: Modifying parameters may obscure data flow and reduce interface clarity.

rules.description: A function identifier shall only be used with either a preceding &, or with a parenthesized parameter list.
rules.notes: Restricting function identifier usage reduces ambiguity between function designators and calls.

rules.description: A pointer resulting from arithmetic on a pointer operand shall address an element of the same array as that pointer operand.
rules.notes: Pointer arithmetic outside the bounds of the same array may result in undefined behavior.

rules.description: Subtraction between pointers shall only be applied to pointers that address elements of the same array.
rules.notes: Pointer subtraction is only meaningful and defined within the same array object.

rules.description: The relational operators >, >=, < and <= shall not be applied to expressions of pointer type except where they point into the same object.
rules.notes: Relational comparison of unrelated pointers is not portable and may be undefined.

rules.description: The +, -, += and -= operators shall not be applied to an expression of pointer type.
rules.notes: Avoiding pointer arithmetic improves readability and reduces address-manipulation errors.

rules.description: Declarations shall contain no more than two levels of pointer nesting.
rules.notes: Deep pointer nesting reduces readability and makes interfaces harder to understand and verify.

rules.description: The address of an object with automatic or thread-local storage shall not be copied to another object that persists after the first object has ceased to exist.
rules.notes: Such copies create dangling references and may cause invalid memory access.

rules.description: Flexible array members shall not be declared.
rules.notes: Flexible array members complicate size analysis and may reduce portability.

rules.description: Variable-length arrays shall not be used.
rules.notes: Variable-length arrays complicate memory analysis and may introduce stack-usage uncertainty.

rules.description: An object with temporary lifetime shall not undergo array-to-pointer conversion.
rules.notes: Using pointers derived from temporary objects may result in invalid references.

rules.description: Pointers to variably-modified array types shall not be used.
rules.notes: Such pointers reduce portability and complicate static analysis.

rules.description: An object shall not be assigned or copied to an overlapping object.
rules.notes: Copying between overlapping objects may produce unexpected results and corrupt data.

rules.description: The union keyword shall not be used.
rules.notes: Unions may obscure the active stored type and complicate interpretation, portability, and verification.

rules.description: #include directives shall only be preceded by preprocessor directives or comments.
rules.notes: This keeps preprocessing structure consistent and easier to review.

rules.description: The ', " or \ characters and the /* or // character sequences shall not occur in a header file name.
rules.notes: Restricting header file names avoids preprocessing ambiguity and improves portability.

rules.description: The #include directive shall be followed by either a <filename> or "filename" sequence.
rules.notes: This restriction avoids preprocessing ambiguity and keeps include usage consistent and portable.

rules.description: A macro shall not be defined with the same name as a keyword.
rules.notes: Using a keyword as a macro name may break readability and interfere with language syntax expectations.

rules.description: Expressions resulting from the expansion of macro parameters shall be appropriately delimited.
rules.notes: Proper delimiting of macro expansions helps prevent unintended operator precedence and evaluation issues.

rules.description: The controlling expression of a #if or #elif preprocessing directive shall evaluate to 0 or 1.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
#define FEATURE_LEVEL 2
#if FEATURE_LEVEL
#endif
/* Compliant */
#define FEATURE_ENABLED 1
#if (FEATURE_ENABLED == 1)
#endif
rules.notes: Restricting preprocessing conditions to 0 or 1 improves clarity and avoids toolchain-dependent interpretations.

rules.description: All identifiers used in the controlling expression of #if or #elif preprocessing directives shall be #define‘d before evaluation.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
#if FEATURE_ENABLED
#endif
/* Compliant */
#define FEATURE_ENABLED 1
#if (FEATURE_ENABLED == 1)
#endif
rules.notes: Undefined identifiers in preprocessing expressions may lead to misleading or unintended conditional compilation.

rules.description: A line whose first token is # shall be a valid preprocessing directive.
rules.notes: Any line beginning with # shall be syntactically valid to avoid preprocessing ambiguity and build-time defects.

rules.description: All #else, #elif and #endif preprocessor directives shall reside in the same file as the #if, #ifdef or #ifndef directive to which they are related.
rules.notes: Preprocessor condition blocks shall remain within the same file to preserve structural clarity and maintainability.

rules.description: Bitfields shall not be used.
rules.notes: Bitfields are implementation-dependent in layout and access behavior and therefore reduce portability.

rules.description: Standard Library functions shall not be used.
rules.rationale: Bare-Metal programming is applied throughout this project. Therefore, only the intended functionality with requirements is used.
rules.notes: In this project, bare-metal implementation is intended; therefore, only explicitly required and controlled functionality shall be used.

rules.description: File names shall be chosen as descriptive and meaningful.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
a.c
x1.h
tmp.c
/* Compliant */
temperatureCalculation.c
sensorCoefficients.h
navWpChk.c
dbgPrint.c
rules.notes: Descriptive file names improve navigation, readability, and long-term maintainability of the codebase.

rules.description: File names shall have two parts, a base name and an extension.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
temperatureCalculation
sensorCoefficients
startup
/* Compliant */
temperatureCalculation.c
sensorCoefficients.h
startup.s
rules.notes: A consistent filename structure simplifies tool usage, review, and project organization.

rules.description: Extension of all implementation files shall be “.c” and extension of all header files shall be “.h” and assembly files shall be “.s”.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
temperatureCalculation.cpp
sensorCoefficients.hpp
startup.asm
/* Compliant */
temperatureCalculation.c
sensorCoefficients.h
startup.s
rules.notes: Standardized extensions improve tool compatibility and make file purpose immediately recognizable.

rules.description: Filenames shall be in camel notation and begin with lowercase letter.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
TemperatureCalculation.c
temperature_calculation.c
temperature-calculation.c

/* Compliant */
temperatureCalculation.c
sensorCoefficients.h
navWpChk.c
rules.notes: Consistent filename style improves readability and reduces naming variability across the project.

rules.description: Any directory name on which project depends shall not include white spaces (tabs, spaces, etc.) or punctuation characters. Only allowable character set for these names are ‘0-9’, (English alphabet) ‘A-Z’, (English alphabet) ‘a-z’, ‘_’.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
Project Files
driver-source
config.v1
TürkçeDizin
/* Compliant */
projectFiles
driver_source
configV1
buildOutput
rules.notes: Restricted directory names improve portability across tools, scripts, and operating systems.

rules.description: In addition, the uniqueness of filenames shall not be due solely to a difference in case.
rules.notes: Case-only distinctions in file names may cause conflicts on case-insensitive file systems.

rules.description: Source and header files (including comment sections) shall not contain special characters (characters other than the ones in the English alphabet, such as characters from Turkish alphabet).
rules.notes: Restricting files to English-alphabet characters improves portability across compilers, editors, and build environments.

rules.description: Source code file names shall be composed of characters from the set of (English alphabet) [a-z], (English alphabet) [A-Z], [0-9] and shall begin with a letter.
rules.example:
/* Non-compliant */
1driver.c
driver-module.c
driver_module.c
config@main.h

/* Compliant */
driverModule.c
configMain.h
adc1Driver.c
rules.notes: Restricting filename characters avoids toolchain issues and improves portability.

rules.description: In naming of identifiers, camel notation shall be used.
rules.notes:
Consistent identifier naming improves readability and makes interfaces easier to review.
Reference to Chapter 6 for Abbreviations and Units.

rules.description:
Names of the following types shall begin with an upper case letter:
• structures,
• type definitions
• enumerated types
rules.notes: Consistent capitalization of type names helps distinguish types from variables and functions.

rules.description:
Names of the following shall begin with a lower case letter: 
• functions
• objects 
• variables
• fields within structures
rules.notes: Consistent lowercase naming for objects and functions improves readability and avoids visual ambiguity.

rules.description: Literal constants shall not be used in code; instead, symbolic constants shall be defined and used.
rules.notes: Symbolic constants make intent explicit and simplify maintenance when values need to change.

rules.description: Global constants shall be all caps with '_' separators.
rules.notes: A consistent format for global constants makes them easy to recognize during implementation and review.

rules.description: Hexadecimal constants shall be represented using uppercase letters.
rules.notes: Uppercase hexadecimal notation improves readability and visual consistency.

rules.description: Identifiers shall not begin with the underscore character ‘_’.
rules.notes: The underscore ‘_’ character may not be seen on screen. And usually mixed up with another identifiers without underscore character. Leading underscores may be visually unclear and may also conflict with reserved implementation identifiers.

rules.description: Built in compiler functions shall not be used.
rules.notes: Compilers may have built in functions. But their requirements or implementations may be different than the intention of usage in the project. Usually, they don’t have requirements but specifications. Compiler built-ins may be compiler-specific and may not provide the required level of traceability or portability.

rules.description: All definitions, declarations, and comments shall be written in English.
rules.notes: A single project language improves readability, collaboration, and review consistency.

rules.description: Literal suffixes shall use uppercase rather than lowercase letters.
rules.notes: Uppercase suffixes are easier to distinguish and reduce confusion with digits such as 1.

rules.description: Tabs shall not be used.
rules.notes: Editors may have different TAB sizes for each different computer environments and may cause scattered unreadable code. Modern editors have “Convert Tabs to Spaces” capability. Tabs may be displayed differently across editors and environments, causing inconsistent formatting.

rules.description: There shall be only one statement per line even though the statements are very closely related.
rules.notes: Limiting one statement per line improves readability and simplifies debugging and review.

rules.description: All uses of the #pragma directive shall be documented by a comment in the source or header file.
rules.notes: The #pragma directive is used to provide compiler-specific features and control the behavior of the program. It allows developers to implement features that may not be available in all compilers, ensuring compatibility across different platforms.

rules.description: Bracing shall be used for all if statements and else statements wrapped in a #if - #else - #endif. The wrapped if statements shall contain both braces and statement(s).
rules.notes: Explicit bracing within conditional compilation blocks prevents structural ambiguity and review mistakes.

rules.description: Any function shall not contain more than 200 source lines of code (SLOCs).
rules.notes: Restricting function length helps preserve readability, reviewability, and modular design. See also (Complexity/ nesting restriction rules)

rules.description: Functions shall not have more than 10 arguments.
rules.notes: Excessive argument counts reduce readability and often indicate that a data structure or interface redesign is needed.

rules.description: Functions shall not be declared more than once.
rules.notes: Repeated declarations may reduce readability and make interface control more difficult during review.

rules.description: Function declarations shall be placed before function definitions.
rules.notes: A single declaration point before the definition improves readability and helps maintain interface consistency.

rules.description: <stdbool.h> shall be used for Boolean data types.
rules.notes: Using standard Boolean definitions improves clarity and avoids project-specific Boolean representations.

rules.description: Signed and unsigned values shall not be mixed in arithmetic or comparison operations.
rules.notes: Mixing signed and unsigned values may produce unintended conversions and comparison results.

rules.description: Function-like macros shall not contain conditional statements.
rules.notes: Conditional logic inside function-like macros may hide control flow and make behavior harder to analyze.

rules.description: No function shall have a cyclomatic complexity greater than 25.
rules.notes: The cyclomatic complexity metric used by the project shall be explicitly defined and applied consistently.

rules.description: Braces shall be placed on a new line aligned with the associated keyword.
rules.notes: A consistent brace placement style improves readability and visual structure.

rules.description: All block indentations shall be at three (3) spaces and be consistent within the same source file.
rules.notes: Consistent indentation improves readability and makes block structure easier to understand.

rules.description: There shall be at least one space before or after each operator to improve readability.
rules.notes: Consistent spacing around operators improves readability and reduces visual parsing errors.

rules.description: For fixed-point arithmetic operations, the Q format of operands and results shall be explicitly identifiable.
rules.notes: Fixed-point conventions shall be explicit so that scaling assumptions remain clear during implementation and review.

rules.description: There shall be at least one space before or after each operator to improve readability.
rules.notes: Consistent spacing around operators improves readability and reduces visual parsing errors.

rules.description: There shall be exactly one space after each comma in a function parameter list, and no space shall be inserted between a function name and the opening parenthesis.
rules.notes: Consistent spacing in parameter and argument lists improves readability and makes function interfaces easier to review.

rules.description: Fixed-point variables shall use a Q<X> suffix, where <X> represents the number of fractional bits.
rules.notes: Including the Q format in the variable name makes scaling and precision assumptions visible to the reviewer.

rules.description: <stdint.h>  shall be used for Fixed-width integer types.
rules.notes: Fixed-width integer types make data size explicit and improve portability across targets. Also see fixed point arithmetic naming conventions.

rules.description: Within a build configuration, a single assembler dialect shall be used; mixing dialects in the same build is forbidden.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Mixed assembler dialects in the same build

; file1.s - GNU as syntax
.syntax unified
.thumb

addOne:
adds r0, r0, #1
bx   lr

; file2.s - ARMASM syntax
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY

subOne PROC
SUB r0, r0, #1
BX  lr
ENDP
END


;==================== Compliant ====================
; Single assembler dialect is used consistently in same build

; file1.s - ARMASM syntax
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
EXPORT addOne

addOne PROC
ADD r0, r0, #1 ; Increment input value in r0 by 1
BX  lr         ;  Return to the caller
ENDP

; file2.s - ARMASM syntax
EXPORT subOne

subOne PROC
SUB r0, r0, #1 ; Decrement input value in r0 by 1
BX  lr         ; Return to the caller
ENDP
END
rules.notes: Using a single assembler dialect throughout the build avoids syntax inconsistency and improves reviewability.

rules.description: Each assembly file shall declare the instruction set state explicitly (e.g. ARM).
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Syntax and instruction set state are not declared explicitly
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
EXPORT addOne

addOne PROC
ADD r0, r0, #1
BX  lr
ENDP
END
;==================== Compliant ====================
; ARMASM syntax is used and Thumb state is declared explicitly
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
ARM
EXPORT addOne

addOne  PROC
ADD r0, r0, #1 ; Increment input value in r0 by 1
BX  lr         ; Return to the caller
ENDP

END
rules.notes: Explicitly declaring the assembly state at the start of each file improves readability and prevents ambiguity during build and review.

rules.description: Tabs shall be avoided; indentation shall be spaces only.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Indentation uses tab characters
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT addOne

addOne  PROC
<TAB>ADD r0, r0, #1
<TAB>BX  lr
ENDP

END
;==================== Compliant ====================
; Indentation uses spaces only
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
ARM
EXPORT addOne

addOne  PROC
ADD r0, r0, #1 ; Increment input value in r0 by 1
BX  lr         ; Return to the caller
ENDP

END
rules.notes: Using spaces only for indentation improves formatting consistency across editors and review tools.

rules.description: One instruction per line shall be used; macro expansions and .macro blocks are permitted only if they improve readability and are documented.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Multiple instructions are placed on the same line
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
ARM
EXPORT addOne
addOne  PROC
ADD r0, r0, #1    MOV r1, r0
BX  lr
ENDP

END
;==================== Compliant ====================
; One instruction is placed on each line
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
ARM
EXPORT addOne
addOne  PROC
ADD r0, r0, #1 ; Add 1 to the input value in r0
MOV r1, r0     ; Copy the updated value from r0 to r1
BX  lr         ; Return to the caller
ENDP

END
rules.notes: Using one instruction per line improves readability and makes review, debugging, and traceability easier.

rules.description: Immediate constants shall be named via EQU, except for {0,1,2,4,8,16,32} used as shift/size/align constants and other explicitly allowlisted values.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Non-trivial immediate constant is used directly

TIMEOUT_EXAMPLE_NONCOMPLIANT PROC
MOV   r0, #100
BX    lr
ENDP
;==================== Compliant ====================
; Non-trivial immediate constant is named with EQU
; Allowlisted small constants remain direct

TIMEOUT_VALUE   EQU   100

TIMEOUT_EXAMPLE_COMPLIANT PROC
MOV   r0, #TIMEOUT_VALUE ; Load named timeout constant
LSLS  r1, r1, #4         ; Shift by allowlisted constant 4
ADDS  r2, r2, #1         ; Increment by allowlisted constant 1
BX    lr                 ; Return to caller
ENDP
rules.notes: Non-trivial immediate constants shall be named so that intent remains explicit during review, while small allowlisted values may be used directly when their meaning is obvious.

rules.description: Any computed branch target shall have bit[0]=0; setting bit[0] is forbidden.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; bit[0] is set, so BX switches to Thumb state

AREA |.text_arm|, CODE, READONLY
ARM
EXPORT branchNonCompliant

branchNonCompliant PROC
LDR   r0, =thumbTarget
ORR   r0, r0, #1
BX    r0
ENDP

AREA |.text_thumb|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB

thumbTarget
BX    lr

;==================== Compliant ====================
; bit[0] is cleared, so BX remains in Arm state
; file: dispatcherJumpTable.s ve ; Allowlisted dispatcher module
AREA |.text_arm2|, CODE, READONLY
ARM
EXPORT branchCompliant

branchCompliant PROC
LDR   r0, =armTarget ; Load computed branch target address
BIC   r0, r0, #1     ; Clear bit[0] of the computed target
BX    r0             ; Branch using the state-valid target
ENDP

armTarget
BX    lr             ; Return to the caller

END
rules.notes:
If the lowest bit is 1, the branch will switch to Thumb state. If the lowest bit is 0, the branch will switch to Arm state. Note that the lowest bit is never actually used as part of the address as all instructions are either 4-byte aligned (as in Arm) or 2-byte aligned (as in Thumb).
This rule applies only to targets where bit[0] is architecturally defined as an execution-state selector.

rules.description: TBB/TBH shall only be used in allowlisted dispatcher modules and shall be preceded by explicit index bounds checking.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; TBB/TBH are used without explicit bounds checking
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT dispatchTbbNonCompliant
EXPORT dispatchTbhNonCompliant
dispatchTbbNonCompliant PROC
ADR   r1, jumpTableByte
TBB   [r1, r0]
jumpTableByte
DCB   0, 1
ENDP
dispatchTbhNonCompliant PROC
ADR   r1, jumpTableHalf
TBH   [r1, r0, LSL #1]
jumpTableHalf
DCW   0, 2
ENDP
END
;==================== Compliant ====================
; TBB/TBH are used only after explicit bounds checking
; file: dispatcherJumpTable.s ve ; Allowlisted dispatcher module
EXPORT dispatchTbbCompliant
EXPORT dispatchTbhCompliant
dispatchTbbCompliant PROC
CMP   r0, #2         ; Compare index against table size
BCS   defaultCaseTbb ; Branch if index is out of range

; Load byte jump table base address
ADR   r1, jumpTableByteCompliant
; Branch through byte table using checked index
TBB   [r1, r0]
defaultCaseTbb
BX    lr        ; Return on default path
jumpTableByteCompliant
DCB   0, 1      ; Define byte table entries
ENDP
dispatchTbhCompliant PROC
CMP   r0, #2            ; Compare index against table size
BCS   defaultCaseTbh    ; Branch if index is out of range
; Load halfword jump table base address
ADR   r1, jumpTableHalfCompliant
; Branch through halfword table using checked index
TBH   [r1, r0, LSL #1]
defaultCaseTbh
BX    lr   ; Return on default path
jumpTableHalfCompliant
DCW   0, 2 ; Define halfword table entries
ENDP
END
rules.notes: By using these instructions, the programmer can control the branch behavior of the program, which is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the dispatcher's logic and preventing potential out-of-bounds or unpredictable behavior. The explicit index bounds checking ensures that the programmer can verify the bounds of the index used in the branch, thus preventing any unintended or incorrect behavior that could compromise the dispatcher's functionality.

rules.description: Direct writes to PC (e.g., mov pc,*, add pc,*, ldr pc,*) shall be prohibited. Function returns shall use only bx lr or pop {...,pc}. Exception returns shall use only architecturally valid bx lr EXC_RETURN sequences.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Direct writes to PC are used
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT jumpNonCompliant
EXPORT returnNonCompliant

jumpNonCompliant PROC
LDR   pc, =targetLabel
ENDP
returnNonCompliant PROC
MOV   pc, lr
ENDP
targetLabel
BX    lr
rules.notes: The prohibition on direct write to the PC in ARM architecture is primarily to enforce a load-store model for memory access. This means that all memory operations must be performed using load (LDR) and store (STR) instructions, rather than directly modifying the program counter.

rules.description: Any assembly function shall not exceed 80 SLOC (excluding blank lines and comments). Exceptions (startup, context switch, vector table) shall be explicitly allowlisted or justified.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Function is too long and exceeds 80 SLOC
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT processDataNonCompliant

processDataNonCompliant PROC
PUSH  {r4-r7, lr}
MOV   r4, r0
MOV   r5, r1
MOV   r6, r2
MOV   r7, r3

ADD   r4, r4, #1
SUB   r5, r5, #1
EOR   r6, r6, r4
ORR   r7, r7, r5
CMP   r4, #0
BEQ   skipBlock1

skipBlock1
; ... many additional instruction blocks ...
; ... total function length exceeds 80 SLOC ...
; ... startup/context-switch/vector-table exception not justified ...

POP   {r4-r7, pc}
ENDP
;==================== Compliant ====================
; Long logic is split into smaller functions below the SLOC limit
EXPORT processDataCompliant
EXPORT processDataPartA
EXPORT processDataPartB

processDataCompliant PROC
PUSH  {lr}               ; Save return address
BL    processDataPartA   ; Execute first part of the logic
BL    processDataPartB   ; Execute second part of the logic
POP   {pc}               ; Return to the caller
ENDP

processDataPartA PROC
ADD   r0, r0, #1         ; Increment r0
SUB   r1, r1, #1         ; Decrement r1
BX    lr                 ; Return to the caller
ENDP

processDataPartB PROC
EOR   r2, r2, r0      ; Apply exclusive-OR using r0 and r2
ORR   r3, r3, r1      ; Apply inclusive-OR using r1 and r3
BX    lr              ; Return to the caller
ENDP

END
rules.notes: Assembly functions should remain small enough for effective review, and any function exceeding the SLOC limit shall be explicitly allowlisted or justified.

rules.description: Each assembly file shall place all code and data into explicit, named sections; implicit/default section placement shall not be relied upon.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Code and data are not both placed into explicit named sections

THUMB
EXPORT readValueNonCompliant

readValueNonCompliant PROC
LDR   r0, =tableValue
LDR   r0, [r0]
BX    lr
ENDP
tableValue
DCD   0x12345678

;==================== Compliant ====================
; Code and data are placed into explicit named sections

AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT readValueCompliant

readValueCompliant PROC
LDR   r0, =tableValueCompliant ; Load address of data obj
LDR   r0, [r0] ; Read data value from memory
BX    lr       ; Return to the caller
ENDP

AREA |.rodata|, DATA, READONLY
tableValueCompliant
DCD   0x12345678   ; Define read-only constant data

END
rules.notes: Sections/segments define where code and data are placed in the object file.

rules.description: Each assembly function/submodule shall include an assembly function prolog.
rules.example:
;====================== Compliant ====================

;----------------------------------------------------------------- 
; FUNCTION NAME:
; moduleTemplate_reverseBytes_u32
;
; PURPOSE:
; Reverses the byte order of a 32-bit unsigned value.
;
; INPUT PARAMETERS:
; r0 Input value to be byte-reversed
;
; OUTPUT PARAMETERS:
; r0 Byte-reversed result
;
; RETURNS:
; r0 Byte-reversed 32-bit value
;
; NOTES:
; Rule 162: Allowlisted module: byteOrder.s
; Rule 162: Deviation record: DEV-ASM-003
; Rule 162: Reviewer approval: Low-level reviewer approved
;
;-----------------------------------------------------------------
; FUNC_BEGIN moduleTemplate_reverseBytes
moduleTemplate_reverseBytes
   REV r0, r0 ; Reverse the byte order of the 32-bit value in r0
   BX lr      ; Return to the caller

; FUNC_END moduleTemplate_reverseBytes
rules.notes: Assembly shall only appear in approved allowlisted modules, and any newly introduced .s file shall be deviation-tracked and approved by a qualified low-level reviewer.

rules.description: Assembly shall only be permitted in allowlisted modules. Any new .s file requires a deviation record and low-level reviewer approval.
rules.example: See the compliant example in Rule 160. For this rule, the allowlisted module name, deviation record, and low-level reviewer approval shall be stated explicitly in the NOTES section of the assembly function/file prolog.
rules.notes: See the compliant example in Rule 160. For this rule, the allowlisted module name, deviation record, and low-level reviewer approval shall be stated explicitly in the NOTES section of the assembly function/file prolog.

rules.description: All labels shall begin in column 1 to be recognized by the assembler.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Label is indented and does not begin in column 1
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_loopExample

moduleTemplate_loopExample
MOV   r0, #3
B     loopStart
+++++loopStart
SUBS  r0, r0, #1
BNE   loopStart
BX    lr

END
;==================== Compliant ====================
; Label begins in column 1
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_loopExampleCompliant
moduleTemplate_loopExampleCompliant
MOV   r0, #3  ; Load loop counter initial value into r0
B     loopStartCompliant ; Branch to the loop label
loopStartCompliant
SUBS  r0, r0, #1 ; Decrement the loop counter
BNE   loopStartCompliant ; Repeat loop while counter is not zero
BX    lr ; Return to the caller

END
rules.notes: Labels shall start in column 1 so they are visually distinct from instructions and are recognized consistently by the assembler and review tools.

rules.description: The comment character shall delimit comments.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Comment is not delimited with the assembly comment character
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_addOne
moduleTemplate_addOne
ADD   r0, r0, #1   /* Non-compliant comment style */
BX    lr
;==================== Compliant ====================
; Comment is delimited with the assembly comment character
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_addOneCompliant
moduleTemplate_addOneCompliant
ADD   r0, r0, #1   ; Compliant comment style
BX    lr           ; Return to the caller
END
rules.notes: Comments shall be introduced with the assembler’s defined comment character so that source lines remain readable and are parsed consistently by the toolchain.

rules.description: Every operation in assembly code shall have a corresponding comment which explains the operation.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Not every operation has a corresponding explanatory comment

AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_addTwo

moduleTemplate_addTwo
ADD   r0, r0, #2
BX    lr

;==================== Compliant ====================
; Every operation has a corresponding explanatory comment

AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_addTwoCompliant

moduleTemplate_addTwoCompliant
ADD   r0, r0, #2   ; Add constant 2 to input value in r0
BX    lr           ; Return to the caller

END
rules.notes: Each assembly operation shall include a brief explanatory comment so that intent remains clear during review and maintenance.

rules.description: All assembly elements shall have a single exit point.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; Multiple exit points are used
AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_checkValue

moduleTemplate_checkValue
CMP   r0, #0
BEQ   returnZero
ADD   r0, r0, #1
BX    lr              ; First exit point

returnZero
MOV   r0, #0
BX    lr              ; Second exit point

;==================== Compliant ====================
; A single exit point is used

AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_checkValueCompliant

moduleTemplate_checkValueCompliant
CMP   r0, #0          ; Compare input value with zero
BEQ   setZero         ; Branch if input is zero
ADD   r0, r0, #1      ; Increment input value
B     exitFunction    ; Branch to single exit point

setZero
MOV   r0, #0          ; Set return value to zero

exitFunction
BX    lr              ; Single exit point

END
rules.notes: Using a single exit point makes assembly control flow easier to review, trace, and verify.

rules.description: All symbols that are defined externally to the assembly element in which they are referenced shall be included using the external statement.
rules.example:
;==================== Non-compliant ====================
; External symbol is referenced without an external declaration

AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_callHelper

moduleTemplate_callHelper
; External function is called without IMPORT
BL    helperFunction
BX    lr


;==================== Compliant ====================
; External symbol is declared explicitly with IMPORT

AREA |.text|, CODE, READONLY
THUMB
EXPORT moduleTemplate_callHelperCompliant
IMPORT helperFunction

moduleTemplate_callHelperCompliant
; External function is declared with IMPORT
; Call the imported external helper function
BL    helperFunction
BX    lr  ; Call the imported external helper function

END
rules.notes: Every externally defined symbol shall be declared explicitly with the external statement so that dependencies remain visible and reviewable.
